organizations.normalization_notes: Army service is a military assignment, not a civilian employer; individual units and transfer dates require person-level evidence.

affiliations.date_precision: The oral history places enlistment in September 1943 and says OSS assignment followed; official Army bulk data agree on a September 1943 entry code. Exact Army-to-OSS transfer date and unit remain unknown.
affiliations.research_notes: The Army was the documented formal military pathway immediately before OSS. Earlier SOE-supported Cretan resistance was not established as paid employment. The last civilian employer before enlistment is unknown.

claims.claim_text: The indexed George J Doundoulakis is linked with high confidence to the brother described in Helias Doundoulakis's oral history.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The NARA index and official Army bulk record have the same full name and a nonshared protected identifier. Helias's National WWII Museum oral history independently describes his brother George in the Cretan resistance, U.S. Army, and OSS sequence.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High: full indexed name and nonshared protected identifier agree with official Army bulk record ordinal 364286; the museum oral history names brother George and the same Army-to-OSS pathway. Box 196 has not been opened.
claims.temporal_assessment: The museum describes Cretan resistance before Army enlistment in September 1943 and OSS recruitment afterward; exact OSS start date needs archival confirmation.
claims.match_notes: The separate Helias index row and consecutive Army bulk record are not merged into George. No employer is inferred from the Army occupation code or the brothers' later careers.

claims.claim_text: George J Doundoulakis enlisted in the U.S. Army before joining the OSS; this was a military pathway, not a civilian employer.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Helias's museum oral history says that he and George enlisted in the Army in September 1943 and then joined OSS after a basic-training waiver. An edited museum podcast transcribes Helias describing both brothers entering the Army; official bulk records show both Army entries.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact-name, nonshared protected Army identifier links indexed George to the official record; the museum identifies Helias's brother George in the same Army-to-OSS sequence.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit sequence in the oral history: resistance work, Army enlistment, then OSS recruitment. Exact transfer date and civilian pre-service employer are not documented.
claims.match_notes: U.S. Army is an immediately preceding military assignment only. Do not count it as civilian employment or classify the earlier Cretan resistance as paid SOE employment.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The index prints Theodore D'Oultremont, Belgian second lieutenant, Box 196. A Comète Kinship Belgium profile for Théodore Robert Elie Joseph Ghislain Marie d'Oultremont describes a Belgian reserve-officer candidate and later OSS liaison, citing Belgian defense dossier OO-46851. The original dossier and Box 196 are not yet inspected, so the candidate is not treated as a settled match or a pre-OSS employer.
person_updates.next_action: Compare Box 196 with Belgian defense dossier OO-46851; determine whether Belgian State Security service preceded or overlapped OSS liaison before assigning an immediate pre-OSS institution. Keep this Theodore separate from Georges, Edouard, and Charles-Emile d'Oultremont.
